title: Decode: DSA exact top-k + DCP merge
shape: D3-32 r24: 96 requests / DP rank (384 verify rows), L≈135K (local ≈33.75K on DCP4), k=3; also r1 (16 rows), r8 (128 rows)
basis: MEASURED microbench (4 GPUs = one DCP4 group on Rhea VR200, decode wiring launch shape, CUDA-graph us/call, relu-like indexer logits, L=135K): in-tree 30.4/45.3/85.7 us per layer at r1/r8/r24 (x24 DSA layers = 0.73/1.09/2.06 ms per step; in-step gap512 B92: 2.26 ms). current_ms = r24 after the in-place tie round (76.3 us x 24). achievable = rhea1n model_rows: r24 1.9 + 7.5 us/layer, r8 0.64 + 6.4, r1 0.08 + 5.9
gap_analysis: Measured (runs/D-TOPK/base1.log, per-row globaltimer stamps + CUPTI): (1) ties at the K-th bf16 key straddle >= 2 ranks on 98% of rows (stats tie_round 1512/1536 at r24, 504/512 r8, 64/64 r1); the in-tree path sends them to the leader state machine: one more streamed key pass (WRITE->offsets 11 us at r24) + tie round (~3-4 us). (2) at r8/r24 the launch shape is bounded by max_model_len (cluster 2/4, segmax 0) so the 3 pre-pass kernels run: r24 pp_hist 9.7 + pp_window 8.7 + pp_win 22-28 us = 41-46 us, i.e. more than the merge kernel itself; r8 5.4 us. (3) the merge kernel is a chain of ~12 serial leader/cluster steps of 1.5-3 us each (r1, staged keys: pass A 3.3, S1 1.0, estimate 1.8, window 2.6, send 1.1, NVLink round 1.8, resolve 1.7, quota 1.7, bitmap 2.3-3, tie round 2.6, write 1.5): 27 us for 4.2K keys per CTA. The NVLink round itself is 1.8 us at r1 and 4.7 us at r24 (send->polled); two rounds (window + ties) are inherent to the stock global-id tie rule unless the tie lists ride on round 1.
inefficiencies: MEASURED: tie round on 98% of rows went through the leader state machine with an extra streamed key pass (fixed: in-place tie round on the WRITE bitmaps, -9.4 us r24, -2 us r8/r1)
MEASURED: pre-pass kernels 41-46 us at r24 (pp_win 22-28 us alone) because launch shape is bounded by max_model_len (keys never staged at r8/r24)
MEASURED: ~12 serial 1.5-3 us steps inside the merge kernel (cluster syncs + leader-only work) -> 27 us at r1 for 4.2K keys/CTA
MEASURED: two NVLink rounds per row (window, ties); round latency 1.8 us (r1) to 4.7 us (r24)
merge kernel PDL off (trtllm-gen consumer reads counts before griddepcontrol.wait); on the critical stream
HYPOTHESIS (checking): bench replays may run below boost clock (GPU idles between reps); re-measuring with warm-up matmuls
